promise: Kogia shapes the interface; Kharbga shapes the rules.

skins.name: Palm & limestone

skins.name: Brick & basalt

skins.name: Kogia ceramic

reactions.name: respect
reactions.meaning: Respect the player and the table.

reactions.name: captured
reactions.meaning: A Soldier is enclosed as a result of the move.

reactions.name: chain-capture
reactions.meaning: The same Soldier must continue while another capture exists.

reactions.name: safe-haff
reactions.meaning: A free, protected Soldier remains mobile.

reactions.name: exchange
reactions.meaning: Defender requests one protected Soldier for two Attacker Soldiers.

reactions.name: blocked
reactions.meaning: No legal adjacent orthogonal house remains.

reactions.name: rematch
reactions.meaning: Smooth the sand and begin another round.

history.title: Old, but not precisely dated
history.body: The Tunisian heritage inventory says the appearance date is difficult to determine; collective memory connects it to the Bey era and Hilalian transmission.

history.title: A board made anywhere
history.body: The 49 houses can be carved in soil or sand, or marked in chalk or white paint on cement.

history.title: Objects become Soldiers
history.body: Date pits, pebbles, brick fragments and bottle caps become two visually distinct armies of equal pieces.

history.title: A circle, not a throne room
history.body: Children, adults and elders play in homes, cafés, markets and shopfronts, often surrounded by advice and spectators.
